query: As of early July 2026, what percentage of Russia's national oil-refining capacity is offline/disabled due to Ukrainian drone strikes?
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's the bottom line on the question:

**As of early July 2026, roughly 30–43% of Russia's national refining capacity was offline/disabled**, with the exact figure depending on methodology and source:

- **~42.7%** — Ukrainian General Staff (July 4), measured by *design/nameplate capacity* disabled. This is the highest figure and an official Ukrainian military claim.
- **20–40%** — Financial Times (July 9), citing independent analyst estimates. More conservative, reflecting genuine uncertainty.
- **~one-third to "nearly half"** — Energy Intelligence (of the ~6.6 million b/d fleet).

Corroborating throughput data (Bloomberg/EA Analytics) show Russian refinery runs collapsed to **~3.91 million b/d in early July 2026 — a 21-year low** (down ~1.4 million b/d year-on-year), consistent with a 40%+ shortfall against nameplate capacity.

**Key caveat:** "Design capacity disabled" ≠ "output lost." Earlier in the campaign (late 2025), ~20% of capacity was disabled but output fell only 3–6% because Russia activated idle units. By July 2026 that buffer was largely exhausted — all 11 major refineries had been hit, including Omsk (~10% of capacity) — which is why the throughput collapse became so severe. The figures are also snapshots that fluctuate as facilities are repaired and re-struck.

key_facts: Ukrainian General Staff (July 4, 2026) claimed strikes disabled 42.74% of Russia's total DESIGNED oil-refining capacity — the highest, official Ukrainian figure.
Financial Times (July 9, 2026), citing analysts, reported strikes may have knocked out between 20% and 40% of refining capacity.
Energy Intelligence reported 'nearly half' of Russia's ~6.6 million b/d refining fleet knocked offline since late February 2026; an earlier tally put it at ~one-third (2.14 million b/d).
Russian refinery runs fell to ~3.91 million b/d in early July 2026 — lowest since March 2005 (21-year low), ~1.4 million b/d below a year earlier (Bloomberg / EA Analytics / Energy Aspects).
Russia's total refining capacity is ~6.6 million b/d, the world's third-largest downstream fleet.
All 11 of Russia's largest refineries have been hit; the Omsk refinery (~10% of national capacity) was struck for the first time on July 6, 2026.
Ukraine reportedly struck at least 24 of Russia's 34 large refineries in ~50 attacks over 100 days (Bloomberg tally).
Design-capacity disabled does not equal output lost: in Aug–Oct 2025, ~20% of capacity was disabled but actual output fell only 3–6% due to idle-unit activation; that buffer is now largely exhausted.
The campaign caused ~$13.5 billion in claimed industry losses since August 2025 (Ukrainian General Staff).
By July 2026 fuel restrictions affected ~50 million people (~35% of Russia's population); Russia banned most gasoline/diesel exports and lowered fuel quality standards from Euro-5 to Euro-3.
